sections.title: Setting
sections.text: Alexandria sits at about 22 m above sea level, in a basin that runs from about -32 m to 339 m. It lies in the Mediterranean dry woodlands and steppe ecoregion. Most of its basin lies in the North Saharan Xeric Steppe and Woodland ecoregion. Its basin also takes in parts of the Nile Delta flooded savanna ecoregion.

sections.title: Climate
sections.text: Across the surrounding basin of about 16,375 km², rainfall averages about 74 mm a year, strongly concentrated, with December the wettest month. Temperatures there average 20.2 °C, from 12.5 °C in January to 26.6 °C in August. Its aridity index of 0.05 falls in the UNEP arid class. Compared with the five basins around it, its basin receives more precipitation than all but one, is cooler than three and is more humid than all but one.

sections.title: Water
sections.text: The basin meets the sea at its outlet, so little water arrives from upstream. Lakes cover about 1% of the basin and wetlands about 2%. The basin drains directly to the sea.

sections.title: Land and geology
sections.text: Across the basin, the land is level on average (a mean slope of 0.9%), with topsoil that averages 52% sand, 30% silt and 18% clay (USDA texture class: loam). The underlying rock is mostly unconsolidated sediments. Karst outcrop covers up to about 100% of the basin.

sections.title: Land cover around 2000
sections.text: Around 2000, about 24% of the basin is cropland and 3% is pasture; in the GLC2000 land cover map, the commonest class other than cultivated land is bare areas, at about 54%. Compared with the five basins around it, its basin has more cropland than all but one and more pasture than three.

sections.title: Surroundings
sections.text: Alexandria's basin is one of six that meet here. None of them drains into it. It drains into none of them. All but one of the basins across its divides are higher. Of the six basins that meet here, it has the most runoff.

sections.title: About these figures
sections.text: The elevation and ecoregion under Setting are for Alexandria itself. The other figures describe the basin of about 16,375 km² that contains it, from global datasets. Elevation and distances are measured from the place's point in WHG, which may be the centre of a town rather than its shore or riverbank.
